# F1 Standings | Antonelli extends championship lead, as Hamilton suffers nightmare

Photo: Race Pictures

Updated: 01:45, 12 Oct

Henry Eccles

Henry Eccles is a freelance Formula 1 journalist for GPblog, covering breaking news, live race blogs, and features across the F1 calendar. Since joining in 2026, he has produced high-volume reporting on the sport’s biggest stories, alongside feature pieces including analysis and historical content.

The Formula 1 championship standings have been updated following the Hungarian Grand Prix, with Max Verstappen taking victory around the Marina Bay Street Circuit.

Championship leader Kimi Antonelli, F1’s youngest ever, has seen his points gap extended following his P3 finish, while closest rival George Russell crossed the line in P9, having had to recover from a P19 start due to a power unit penalty.

Antonelli's 340 points in the Drivers' standings now means he can mathematically win the world championship at the next race, set to take place in Austin.

Lewis Hamilton, the highest-placed non-Mercedes driver in the championship battle this season, suffered a nightmare Singapore GP. Opting for a one-stop strategy that saw him on old soft tyres at the end, Hamilton lost his P3 starting position, and ultimately finished P6 - losing a place to Oscar Piastri on the final lap. Verstappen is now only eight points behind his old rival, currently sat P3 in the standings.

## Red Bull pile pressure on McLaren

As for the Constructors’ Standings, Mercedes maintain their lead in the title fight after securing 11 wins from the opening 17 rounds of F1 2026, but it was a strong points haul yet again for Red Bull following Verstappen's second successive Grand Prix victory - and his first-ever around Marina Bay.

Ferrari gain important points from Charles Leclerc's P2 finish, seven seconds behind Verstappen at chequered flag, but Hamilton's P6 means it was a day to forget for the Scuderia.

Despite finishing P4 and P5 in Singapore, McLaren's grip on P3 in the standings is loosening, with Red Bull now seven points away from the papaya team, as Isack Hadjar scored the final point of the race with a recovery drive from the very back of the pit lane.

The Formula One World Championship is one of the most prestigious and exciting motorsports events in the world. It's a thrilling, high-speed competition that pits the world's best drivers against each other in a battle for the championship title. At the heart of the competition are the F1 standings, which allow fans to keep track of each driver's progress throughout the season. 

## F1 driver standings 2026

At the end of the season, the driver with the most points is crowned the Formula One World Champion. The standings also determine the finishing order for the drivers who don't win the championship. The driver who finishes in second place in the standings is referred to as the runner-up, and the driver who finishes in third place is referred to as the third-placed driver, and so on. 

The F1 standings are updated after each race, allowing fans to keep track of their favorite drivers throughout the season. Fans can also use the standings to predict who is most likely to win the championship title. They can also use the standings to follow the progress of drivers from their home country, or to track the performance of the team that they support. 

## F1 constructor standings 2026

In addition to the driver standings, there are also constructor standings. The construction standings are calculated in the same way as the driver standings, with points awarded based on the finishing positions of the team's drivers. The constructor with the most points at the end of the season is crowned the Constructors' Champions. 

In summary, the F1 standings are an essential part of the Formula One World Championship. They allow fans to keep track of each driver's progress throughout the season, and they determine the winner of the championship title. Understanding the F1 standings is essential for fans who want to fully appreciate the excitement and drama of this incredible motorsport.

# When will Kimi Antonelli win the 2026 F1 championship? How he can win at the US GP

Dominic Tobin

October 11, 2026

 October 11th 2026 - Last updated: October 12th 2026

## Kimi Antonelli leads the F1 title race by 102 points after the Singapore GP and could be crowned Formula 1's youngest-ever world champion at the very next race. But six drivers can still take the F1 title — here are the permutations

 Grand Prix Photo 

Dominic Tobin

October 11, 2026

Kimi Antonelli can win the Formula 1 World Championship at the very next race in the United States after extending his title lead once more at the Singapore Grand Prix.

With a 102 point advantage, and a maximum of 150 points to be won, the Mercedes driver is closing in on the trophy. Victory at Circuit of the Americas (COTA) could secure that as soon as October 25 if his team-mate George Russell finishes ninth or lower, and Lewis Hamilton can’t end the race in at least fourth place.

Even Antonelli seemed surprised when told of the news after his third-place finish at Marina Bay. “Can I, really!?” he exclaimed.

With Russell’s recent fortunes, championship victory in the US isn’t unthinkable: the last two rounds have seen him pulling over to the side of the track in Malaysia with power unit failure; spinning out of the lead of the Singapore sprint race and hitting the wall, then finishing ninth in the Grand Prix after starting from the back, having had to take another engine penalty.

However, based on both drivers’ average scoring rates, it’s more likely that Antonelli will be crowned at the Mexico City Grand Prix on November 1 when he’ll be 20 years and 68 days old; he would be t he youngest F1 champion in history, taking that accolade from Sebastian Vettel by more than three years.

He won’t be sizing up a bigger trophy cabinet just yet: nothing can be taken for granted in F1. There are still six drivers mathematically in contention for the title, although nothing short of a catastrophe would see any of Antonelli’s rivals winning – even given Max Verstappen‘s track record of comebacks.

Here is how the 2026 title can be decided, from the most likely outcome to the unprecedented scenarios that would need a minor miracle.

## Who can still win the 2026 F1 championship?

While six drivers might be in contention, that list is likely to get much shorter very quickly.

If Antonelli wins the US Grand Prix, all but Lewis Hamilton and George Russell would be eliminated from the title race, no matter where they finish.

Lando Norris and Charles Leclerc are in a particularly precarious situation, trailing as they are by 139 and 125 points respectively. If they don’t gain on Antonelli at the next race, they will be out of contention.

In this scenario, Antonelli would be champion in the event of a points tie because he’d always have more race wins than anybody else.

results.title: F1 2026 title battle: How Antonelli can clinch the championship in Austin
results.author: Daniel Morgan
results.text:
F1 2026 title battle: How Antonelli can clinch the championship in Austin

Kimi Antonelli heads to Austin with a 102-point lead over George Russell in the 2026 F1 Drivers’ Championship. Editorial illustration: Tech Torque Media.

# F1 2026 title battle: How Antonelli can clinch the championship in Austin

Antonelli leads Russell by 102 points with six races left. We explain the Austin title maths, Mercedes' challenge and Verstappen's threat.

- Daniel Morgan
- 13 October 2026
- Motorsport

Max Verstappen won in Singapore, but the result may be remembered just as much for what it did to the championship. Kimi Antonelli finished third, George Russell came home ninth and the gap between the Mercedes drivers grew to 102 points.

With six Grands Prix left, Antonelli could clinch his first world title at the United States Grand Prix on 25 October. The arithmetic favours him, but Austin isn’t a coronation: Russell can still delay the decision.

## Antonelli’s lead did not happen overnight

Antonelli heads to Texas with 340 points. Russell has 238, with Lewis Hamilton third on 229. Verstappen follows on 221, ahead of Charles Leclerc on 215 and Lando Norris on 201 in the drivers’ championship standings. Russell is now only nine points clear of Hamilton, yet 102 behind his own team-mate.

Antonelli’s season has been built on more than avoiding trouble. He fought through the field to win at Monza, then added another victory at the Spanish Grand Prix in Madrid. Those results gave him room to absorb weekends when the Mercedes was not the fastest car.

Russell has shown the speed to beat him. His Azerbaijan Grand Prix victory was a reminder of that. The difficulty has been putting together enough weekends like Baku to close the gap.

Singapore hurt his chances again. Russell crashed in the wet Sprint and started Sunday’s race from the back following penalties. He fought back to ninth on Sunday, taking two Grand Prix points against Antonelli’s 15. That 13-point swing in the race alone was particularly damaging this late in the season.

## How can Antonelli win the championship in Austin?

Singapore hosted the final Sprint of 2026, leaving six Grands Prix and a maximum of 150 points available. Once Austin is complete, only five races — worth up to 125 points — will remain.

Antonelli therefore needs to leave Austin more than 125 points ahead of every remaining challenger to be uncatchable outright. A victory in Texas would take him to 365 points. If Russell fails to score, he would trail by 127 points; Hamilton would also need to finish fifth or lower to remain more than 125 points behind. Formula 1’s published permutations also allow Russell to finish ninth, with the championship then depending on the applicable countback.

A gap of exactly 125 points could still leave the title dependent on countback, beginning with race wins. Formula 1 has also set out the official title permutations. For Russell, the priority is unmistakable: he needs a major points swing in Texas.

For Antonelli, there is no reason to throw away a strong points finish trying to force a victory. If the championship is still undecided on Sunday evening, he will have another five races to complete the job.

## Russell needs help from the rest of the grid

Even winning in Austin would not guarantee Russell a large points gain. If Antonelli finishes second, the gap closes by only seven points. That is nowhere near enough to put the championship back in Russell’s hands.

Russell needs other drivers between himself and Antonelli, or a rare scoreless weekend for the championship leader. Verstappen, the Ferraris and the McLarens are all capable of getting involved at the front, but Russell cannot choose which Mercedes they finish ahead of.

F1 Standings 2026: Antonelli's Points Lead Over Russell Before Austin

Author: Dewy Ho — VP, Product Experience

# F1 Standings 2026: Antonelli's Points Lead Over Russell Before Austin

Kimi Antonelli leads Mercedes teammate George Russell by 89 points with six races left in 2026. Full F1 drivers and constructors standings, the title math, and what's left on the calendar.

Tuesday, October 13, 2026 5 min read

## F1 Standings 2026: Antonelli's Lead Looks Close to Unbeatable

The f1 standings 2026 picture after the Singapore sprint is about as lopsided as this championship has looked all year. Andrea Kimi Antonelli sits at 325 points, 89 clear of Mercedes teammate George Russell, with six races remaining on a calendar that runs through Abu Dhabi on Dec. 6. That gap is larger than the points on offer at some individual Grands Prix, and it is why the title conversation has shifted from if to when.

### Full Drivers' Championship Standings

1. Andrea Kimi Antonelli, Mercedes, 325 2. George Russell, Mercedes, 236 3. Lewis Hamilton, Ferrari, 221 4. Charles Leclerc, Ferrari, 197 5. Max Verstappen, Red Bull, 196 6. Lando Norris, McLaren, 189 7. Oscar Piastri, McLaren, 128 8. Isack Hadjar, Red Bull, 96 9. Liam Lawson, Racing Bulls, 69 10. Pierre Gasly, Alpine, 41

Mercedes has turned 2026 into a two car duel at the front, and Russell leads Hamilton by just 15 points for second, with Hamilton holding a 24 point cushion over Leclerc for third. That midfield fight for the final podium spot in the standings is tighter than anything happening at the top.

Further down the order, the rookie class is where the real development story sits. Isack Hadjar's 96 points for Red Bull and Liam Lawson's 69 for Racing Bulls both outpace where most first and second year drivers land in a season dominated by one team the way Mercedes has dominated this one, and both are candidates to climb another tier or two before the calendar runs out.

### Constructors' Championship Standings

1. Mercedes, 561 2. Ferrari, 418 3. McLaren, 317 4. Red Bull, 306 5. Racing Bulls, 94

Mercedes has already built a 143 point cushion over Ferrari in the constructors' table, which, combined with Antonelli's lead, makes Sunday afternoons this fall less about who wins the title and more about when the math closes the door. McLaren and Red Bull are separated by just 11 points for third, and that battle has a direct bearing on next year's prize money and wind tunnel allocation, even with the top of the table decided.

### The Title Math

Antonelli does not need to win every remaining race to close this out. With 89 points separating him from Russell and a maximum of 26 available per race weekend between the win, fastest lap, and sprint points, the gap is already larger than what Russell could make up in a single clean weekend. A top five finish for Antonelli at the United States Grand Prix on Oct. 25, paired with anything less than a win for Russell, starts shrinking the number of races Mercedes even needs to play out. Barring a multi race mechanical collapse, Antonelli is positioned to clinch before the Las Vegas round on Nov. 21, let alone Abu Dhabi.

### What's Left on the 2026 Calendar

United States Grand Prix, Austin, Oct. 25

Mexico City Grand Prix, Nov. 1

Sao Paulo Grand Prix, Brazil, Nov. 8

Las Vegas Grand Prix, Nov. 21

Qatar Grand Prix, Nov. 29

Abu Dhabi Grand Prix, Dec. 6

Six races remain, including three in a four week stretch from late October through mid November that will do most of the heavy lifting on the final standings. That stretch also includes two of the calendar's highest degree of difficulty venues in Mexico City's altitude and the Las Vegas street circuit, either of which could produce the kind of result that reshuffles the midfield more than the top of the order.

### Betting and Fantasy Impact

With the title race effectively a formality, the sharper angle for the rest of 2026 is the fight for second and the constructors' battle for the final podium
